claims.text: In multi-component concentrated alloys, strength is primarily controlled by local fluctuations in shear-fault energy.
The local shear-fault-energy fluctuations arise from chemically driven short-range order.
Short-range order creates hard local atomic motifs that pin dislocations.
Local hard motifs force dislocations onto wavy and jumpy slip paths.
Resistance from local shear-fault-energy fluctuations raises alloy strength.
Rapid quenching can produce a nearly random NiCoCr or related alloy with minimal short-range order.
Low-temperature annealing below complete disordering can increase short-range order while retaining the same overall composition and grain size.
The proposed comparison holds composition and grain size constant between rapidly quenched and annealed specimens.
Chemical short-range order produces spatial variations in the local shear-fault or stacking-fault energy landscape.
The spatially heterogeneous energy landscape contains high-barrier regions within a relatively random matrix.
Local fluctuations in fault energy provide dislocation resistance in concentrated alloys.
Pinning by the heterogeneous energy landscape causes nanoscale dislocation-segment detrapping and wavy or jumpy motion.
Dislocation pinning increases the critical resolved shear stress and consequently the macroscopic yield strength.
Relative to the rapidly quenched baseline, an SRO-enhanced annealed sample will have higher yield strength.
Relative to the rapidly quenched baseline, an SRO-enhanced annealed sample will show more wavy or discontinuous dislocation configurations by TEM.
A rapidly quenched specimen with minimal SRO has a more uniformly averaged fault-energy landscape.
The hypothesis is expected to apply only when changing SRO does not induce secondary phases.
At sufficiently high temperature, thermally activated recovery can mask the proposed pinning effect.
Fault-energy fluctuations may contribute on the order of 50% of the critical resolved shear stress.
Resistance from local fault-energy fluctuations can dominate strengthening from elastic misfit of alloying elements.
